Subject: MSA redlines - EU data processor carveout request

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team ran a redline and flagged the indemnity section. Because NovaPro operates solely as a data processor in the EU for several of our public sector customers, our counsel is asking for a carveout to avoid taking on IP indemnity for third-party claims that arise solely from customer-provided training data or from processing instructions.

High-level ask: add a narrowly-tailored exception so that NovaPro is not required to indemnify Redwood (or third parties) for claims that relate only to Customer Data where NovaPro is acting as a processor under EU law, and where NovaPro followed Customer instructions and used only Customer-supplied models or data.

We also proposed a modest notification/evidence timeline and suggested language to limit damages to direct losses and exclude punitive damages. We attached the redline and a short note from our counsel explaining the EU data-protection rationale.

Can we get your legal team’s read tomorrow? We’re trying to stay on the procurement calendar for an April 15th go-live and this is the last material blocker.

Best,
Arielle Simon
VP, Strategic Partnerships
NovaPro Technologies

Team —

Thanks for the heads-up, Jonas. Read NovaPro’s redline and counsel note. High-level legal position and suggested compromise below:

1) We can accept a narrowly-drawn processor carveout with the following guardrails:
   - It only applies where Customer Data is the sole basis of the third-party claim (i.e., the alleged infringement arises solely from Customer-supplied data or instructions).
   - NovaPro must demonstrate (i) the specific customer instruction(s) in effect at the relevant time, and (ii) an internal processing log showing the content/inputs used.
   - Carveout does NOT apply where NovaPro (a) modified or combined Customer Data with third-party models, (b) deployed additional model weights or code that were not Customer-supplied, or (c) offered outputs under their own branding as a product.

2) Cap & damages: we should push back on deleting consequential/punitive exclusions. Compromise: maintain standard cap (e.g., total fees paid in prior 12 months) but permit a narrower cap for processor-only claims (e.g., lesser of fees in prior 6 months or $250k) — this acknowledges the limited exposure while protecting Redwood on product-origin claims.

3) Notice & evidence: propose 30 days to provide initial notice, 45 days for a validated evidence bundle; if NovaPro cannot produce the bundle in 45 days, Redwood can move to defense or settlement steps and seek reimbursement only for demonstrable obligations. Evidence checklist: customer instruction (contract or signed SOW), processing logs with timestamps, model/version hashes, deployment manifest, and sample inputs/outputs (redact PII as needed).

4) Defensive control: we should retain the right to assume defense for claims involving Redwood-owned models or code. For processor-only claims (as defined above) where NovaPro provides the required evidence, Redwood can agree to defer to NovaPro for initial handling with Redwood’s right to step in if technical evidence suggests product-origin.

If team is aligned, I can draft specific redline text and an email to Arielle with two options: (A) our preferred language (tight carveout + evidence requirements + cap), and (B) a concession language (slightly broader carveout but higher evidence burden and shorter notice). I recommend we offer Option B only if they accept the shorter cap and a categorical exclusion for punitive damages remains.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Arielle —

Thanks for the redline and the quick turnaround. Our legal team reviewed and can accept a narrowly-tailored EU processor carveout with the guardrails Kim proposed (see summary below). The two practical asks from Redwood: (1) we need the evidence checklist populated for any claim relying on the carveout; and (2) agreement to a reduced cap specifically for processor-only claims.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly will send formal redline text with Alternative A/B by end of day tomorrow.
- If NovaPro accepts one of the alternatives, Marissa will update the order form and we’ll route for procurement signoff; we’ll also include the DocuSign link in follow-up.
- If you want us to consider a slightly broader carveout, we’ll need your counsel to confirm the processing role in each target contract and provide a short attestation template we can include in the order form.

If April 15th is still on the table, let us know ASAP; otherwise we’ll schedule a 30-minute legal touchpoint for Friday morning to finalize language.

Best,
Jonas Weber
